quotes.text: an iDT – a human–AI system which visualizes physical SCs in digital form, collects and processes data for modelling using analytics methods, mimics human decision-making rules, and creates new knowledge and decision-making algorithms through human–AI collaboration
quotes.section: 2.2 Cognitive digital twins and human–artificial intelligence collaboration (also Abstract, 1 Introduction, 5 Conclusions)

quotes.text: An iDT describes an SC (e.g. facility locations, demand points, warehouses, suppliers, production and logistics processes). Humans define decision-making and operational practices (e.g. multiple sourcing) as well as decision-making rules and algorithms (e.g. stock replenishment rules).

AI in the iDT can perform traditional expert system tasks (i.e. replicating decision rules coded by humans) and discover their own decision-making rules using training data. AI improves itself and extends the human's metaknowledge.

The iDT concept builds upon traditional digital twins and CDTs explicitly stating that both humans and AI can be knowledge-creating and decision-making units in that they can collaborate, mutually learn from each other, and delegate decision-making tasks to each other.

We stress that iDTs do not aim at fully automated decision making but rather strive for a combination of human and AI from the ‘human in the loop’ perspective, where the ‘human [remains] an integral part of AI decision making’

AI algorithms usually outperform humans in standardized tasks. However, humans have experience and creativity, which create complementary knowledge to AI algorithms for non-standardized situations. Second, human abilities on delegating tasks to others, including AI, depend on their metaknowledge
